quotes.speaker: Jaylen Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Jaylen Brown on managing his ADHD and diverse interests
quotes.excerpt: I think I like master ADHD. I think it has a lot largely to do with my ADHD.
quotes.quote: I love to learn. I think that's the most important thing. I love to explore. I think this is just a part of my curious nature to go learn different things. But in reality, I think I like master ADHD. I think it has a lot largely to do with my ADHD. It's like when my meter fills up in one thing, I just go to the next thing, and then I just go to the next thing, and then I just go to the next thing. So, I think it has a lot largely to do with my ADHD, but that's why you see me doing so many different things because my brain is always moving at 100 miles per hour.

quotes.speaker: Daniel Radcliffe
quotes.summary_phrase: Daniel Radcliffe on the pressures of early fame
quotes.excerpt: Everyone else that I knew and grew up, a lot of young actors that I grew up knowing, were looking for the thing that made them super famous.
quotes.quote: I've been put in a position because of Harry Potter and because of what that did for my career really early where I didn't have to. Everyone else that I knew and grew up, a lot of young actors that I grew up knowing, were looking for the thing that made them super famous. Because what having that kind of name recognition does in our industry is it just it gives you choice. You can choose what you want to do next. You don't have to just do a job for money or do a job because your agents are telling you that it's the thing to do. You can do it because you love it.

quotes.speaker: Daniel Radcliffe
quotes.summary_phrase: Daniel Radcliffe on the challenges of being a young actor
quotes.excerpt: Towards the end of the films, I started getting all of us started getting the question a lot from journalists of like, what are you going to do after this?
quotes.quote: Towards the end of the films, I started getting all of us started getting the question a lot from journalists of like, what are you going to do after this? Basically the implication was, well, you're fucked now, aren't you? What are you going to do after this? There's nothing left. And you know, actually as I look back and I'm like, I can't believe people were saying that kind of stuff to a teenager. Like this is a really crazy thing to say to a young person.

quotes.speaker: Daniel Radcliffe
quotes.summary_phrase: Daniel Radcliffe on directors who wanted to reinvent him
quotes.excerpt: I would like him in my movie because I want to be the person that like reinvents him.
quotes.quote: For every one of those directors there was, there was also a director that went, oh I would like him in my movie because I want to be the person that like reinvents him or that can show an audience this actor that they think they know in a different light. The first film I did in New York was called Kill Your Darlings, and it's about Alan Ginsberg. That director was a guy called John Krokidas, who's fantastic, and he was really like, I want to show you in this different light.

quotes.speaker: Jaylen Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Jaylen Brown on the challenges of being an NBA player
quotes.excerpt: It's very hard to make it to the NBA. It's like you're in the 1% of the 1% but in the very similar facet, you can be typecasted.
quotes.quote: I feel the same way being a basketball player. It's very hard to make it to the NBA. It's like you're in the 1% of the 1% but in the very similar facet, you can be typecasted where it's like you're just a basketball player. And throughout my career, I think I've I've done a good job of making sure that I've tried to not fight but develop other aspects of me so people can see that I was more than just a basketball player.

quotes.speaker: Daniel Radcliffe
quotes.summary_phrase: Daniel Radcliffe on the pressure of being a child star
quotes.excerpt: You have to figure out what of that is like not real and what you actually are and what you actually want.
quotes.quote: Part of growing up famous is that as you are trying to figure out who you are, you are getting this like perceived version of yourself reflected back at you from like a million places and a million people all the time. And so you have to figure out what of that is like not real and what you actually are and what you actually want.

quotes.speaker: Jaylen Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Jaylen Brown on the short career span of NBA players
quotes.excerpt: The average for NBA players is four years, four and a half years, and it's only getting younger and younger.
quotes.quote: It is a small window. Actually the average for NBA players is four years, four and a half years, and it's only getting younger and younger. So I'm in my 10th season, so I'm already blessed to make it to where I'm at. I'm double the the the average and you you never know when the the ball can stop. It's not necessarily always up to you. You just got to make sure you stay in shape and stay in talent.

quotes.speaker: Jaylen Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Jaylen Brown on supporting the mental health of NBA players
quotes.excerpt: A lot of athletes deal with a lot of mental health, like NBA players. I help with I work with the Union.
quotes.quote: A lot of athletes deal with a lot of mental health, like NBA players. I help with I work with the Union, so I kind of help with you know, the transition of of being a NBA player into like other aspects and developing that. I think that's very important. So for me, I think I've done it at such a early age. I started at 18 and I encourage players, start as soon as you come in, think about the end in the beginning.

quotes.speaker: Jaylen Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Jaylen Brown on the lack of governance in NIL deals
quotes.excerpt: There's no governance, you know, amongst our youth. So like an agent can sign a kid to like a 360 deal.
quotes.quote: In basketball, there's the emergence of name, image and likeness. So now kids can go to college and get paid. But what happens is there's no governance, you know, amongst our youth. So like an agent can sign a kid to like a 360 deal. And by the time he's 18 or he's still signed to this shitty deal and something like that. It happens, you know, and we try to are trying to figure out ways to build parameters around it.

quotes.speaker: Jaylen Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Jaylen Brown on the power of sports to connect people
quotes.excerpt: It's also a very spiritual game. People feel connected to sports when they watch.
quotes.quote: It's also a very spiritual game. People feel connected to sports when they watch. They feel connected to their favorite players. It can bring people together. It can bring enemies together. So there's a power in sports that that gets denounced in today's time because of analytics. Analytics have like largely drove the game into a direction, but it denotes the connection that people have and the the ability to bring people together. You can't there's no analytics sheet for that.

quotes.speaker: Jaylen Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Jaylen Brown on managing the stress of being a high-performance athlete
quotes.excerpt: I love to travel or to like to kind of break my algorithm, see different things.
quotes.quote: I love to travel or to like to kind of break my algorithm, see different things. Like I said, I love to learn and try different things. You know, I have ADHD. I like master ADHD at this point, where I do all these different activities, but it's also needed in order for my mental health to be stable enough to kind of deal with some of the things that that come with, you know, your your platform or come with being a high-performance thing, high-performance athlete, player, being famous, you know what I mean, to get away from, you know, civilization and all these different things, sometimes to kind of give you in your mind, your nervous system a reset.

quotes.speaker: Daniel Radcliffe
quotes.summary_phrase: Daniel Radcliffe on his regret over camera phones
quotes.excerpt: If I could delete one thing from history, I think it would be the camera phone.
quotes.quote: If I could delete one thing from history, I think it would be the camera phone. Just because for me growing up, I was, you know, when you're doing all the teenage stuff that you want to do and I was so aware of like, I feel like I sympathize a lot with the current generation who are growing up where everyone's constantly worried about something being put on the internet forever and and what you do at a party goes, you know, gets back to your parents or whatever.

quotes.speaker: Daniel Radcliffe
quotes.summary_phrase: Daniel Radcliffe on the importance of not caring about fame
quotes.excerpt: I became really good at like not really caring about any of it.
quotes.quote: I became really good at like not really caring about any of it. And I think you for me, I think there was something really important about realizing that there's nothing about me that is making this happen. I am not special, and I say that in a very positive thing, that there's no like this would be happening to anyone if they had played Harry Potter. So I I got sort of quite good at like not believing in it too much, but also not letting it bother me.

quotes.speaker: Daniel Radcliffe
quotes.summary_phrase: Daniel Radcliffe on his experience with paparazzi
quotes.excerpt: I was, you know, I looked like shit every time I was leaving so they get photos of me looking terrible.
quotes.quote: I was, you know, I looked like shit every time I was leaving so they get photos of me looking terrible. And then at some point, I realized that that the paparazzi had not come because the pictures were worthless because they all looked like they were from the same night. So I was like, great, I'll just wear this same jacket and these same jeans every night for the next three months and and and they stopped bothering me.

quotes.speaker: Jaylen Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Jaylen Brown on the importance of being coachable
quotes.excerpt: I think one that I've seen that is very effective is like being able to treat the top.
quotes.quote: I think one that I've seen that is very effective is like being able to treat the top or like being a harder coach on the top against people who are like more have more credentials than the bottom. Because like I think like the the people who are at the top have the opportunity to influence the rest and also are going to steer the ship. But in NBA, it's a lot of egos. It's a lot of money, it's a lot of emotions, and it's like politics. Coaches are afraid sometimes to challenge their top player because they might if it goes shit, they might lose their job. And job security is is very important. You know, and I can understand that. But if you want to build a winning environment and like you want to maintain the integrity of your group, you got to treat the top is just like you treat the bottom. If anything, you got to be, you know, the top got to be more willing to be coached. You hear great examples like with the Spurs with Gregg Popovich and Tim Duncan.

quotes.speaker: Jaylen Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Jaylen Brown on the importance of collaboration for winning
quotes.excerpt: When we started to get into the finals and we won, it was because it was more collaboration.
quotes.quote: When we started to get into the finals and we won, it was because it was more collaboration. It was more about the team. It was more about the group. And we still have great talent and capacity to lead a group. But I think, you know, um, when we started to get into the finals and we won, it was because it was more collaboration.

quotes.speaker: Daniel Radcliffe
quotes.summary_phrase: Daniel Radcliffe on the importance of listening on set
quotes.excerpt: A director's job on a set is as much about like yes there's a thing that they have to do.
quotes.quote: A director's job on a set is as much about like yes there's a thing that they have to do, there's a job that they have to do, but on the way to doing that job, the real job is like learning how everybody works. Like learning how all the actors work differently, how all the people on set work differently and learning the best way to talk to all of them because one person's process is different from another person's process. I did another job with somebody once and he this is a director called Alex Aja, he's amazing French director. He's he's the good one I'm talking about, not the not the bad one that I'm not naming. But he very quickly somebody had an idea where they were like, hey, what if we did it was a film set around there were like some biblical stuff in the film and so this person had the idea to make all the characters cars have license plates that were Bible verses that were like secret things about their characters and the director was like, oh that's awesome, let's let's do that. And as soon as everyone saw that, everyone was like, oh, we're going to be if we have ideas, they get listened to and they just end up in the film at which point everyone starts like working really hard and pouring themselves into it.
